nodes.characterization_summary: SEM studies showed no observable additional Li chunks on either the Si surface or Li metal surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) studies showed no observable additional Li chunks on either the Si surface or Li metal surface (fig. S3).

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS results for both Si and Li showed minor differences of the SEI components before and after the pulse.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) results for both Si (fig. S4) and Li (fig. S5) showed minor differences of the SEI components before and after the pulse.

nodes.characterization_summary: Cryo-TEM studies measured a similar SEI thickness of ~50 nm in the pre- and postpulse samples and revealed no visible morphological differences in the SEI.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Cryo-transmission electron microscopy (cryo-TEM) studies measured a similar SEI thickness of ~50 nm in the pre- and postpulse samples and revealed no visible morphological differences in the SEI (fig. S6).

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ SEM observations showed movement of isolated Li_xSi particle under nonuniform electric field, attracted to the tungsten tip.
nodes.evidence_snippet: To visualize the migration of isolated Li_xSi under the voltage pulse, we first performed in situ SEM to visualize the movement of a single isolated Li_xSi particle under the nonuniform electric field (Fig. 4A and fig. S12).

nodes.characterization_summary: PALS-measured zeta potentials of Li_xSi particles in electrolyte exhibit substantial variation from positive to negative (average -82.88 mV for Si nanoparticles in water), confirming neutral particle characteristics.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 3D illustrates that the measured zeta potentials of both i-Li_xSi in the electrolyte and Si nanoparticles in toluene exhibit a substantial variation from positive to negative. By contrast, the zeta potential measurement of Si nanoparticles in water (pH = 7) yielded consistent results, averaging at -82.88 mV.
